title: chrysanthemum leucanthemum var. maximum
intro: Chrysanthemum leucanthemum var. maximum, commonly known as White Shasta Daisy, is a flowering plant in the daisy family (Asteraceae). It has been used in traditional medicine, particularly in Chinese and Ayurvedic practices, due to its potential health benefits, which include reducing inflammation, relieving fever, and acting as an antiseptic and antimicrobial agent. The therapeutic actions of White Shasta Daisy include anti-inflammatory, antipyretic, and antiseptic properties, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids. These bioactive compounds are believed to contribute to the plant's therapeutic effects, although further research is needed to fully understand its medicinal properties.
